test_cases.title: Phishing-resistant authentication option availability at AAL2
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is registered and configured for AAL2 authentication.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid company representative credentials.
test_cases.assumptions: The system is configured to support at least one phishing-resistant method (e.g., FIDO2/WebAuthn) as per NIST SP 800-63B-4 §3.2.5.

steps.action: Navigate to the login page for the company representative portal.
steps.expected: The login interface displays at least one authentication option that is phishing-resistant (e.g., 'Sign in with Security Key' or 'Use Biometric/Passkey').

steps.action: Select the phishing-resistant authentication option and complete the authentication process using a valid registered device.
steps.expected: The system successfully authenticates the user and grants access to the portal, confirming the option is functional and meets AAL2 requirements.

test_cases.title: Authentication with multi-factor authenticator
test_cases.preconditions: A registered company representative account exists with a multi-factor authenticator (e.g., TOTP app or hardware token) configured.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid username, valid password, valid MFA code.
test_cases.assumptions: The system supports TOTP as a multi-factor authenticator method.

steps.action: Enter the valid username and password for the company representative.
steps.expected: The system prompts for the second factor (multi-factor authenticator).

steps.action: Enter the valid code from the multi-factor authenticator.
steps.expected: The system authenticates the user successfully and grants access to the portal.

test_cases.title: Authentication with two separate factors
test_cases.preconditions: A registered company representative account exists configured to use two separate factors (e.g., password and SMS OTP).
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid username, valid password, valid SMS OTP.
test_cases.assumptions: The system supports SMS OTP as a separate authentication factor.

steps.action: Enter the valid username and password for the company representative.
steps.expected: The system sends an OTP to the registered phone number and prompts for it.

steps.action: Enter the valid OTP received via SMS.
steps.expected: The system authenticates the user successfully and grants access to the portal.

test_cases.title: Authentication failure with invalid MFA code
test_cases.preconditions: A registered company representative account exists with a multi-factor authenticator configured.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid username, valid password, invalid MFA code.

steps.action: Enter the valid username and password for the company representative.
steps.expected: The system prompts for the second factor.

steps.action: Enter an invalid code from the multi-factor authenticator.
steps.expected: The system rejects the authentication attempt and displays an error message.

test_cases.title: Authentication failure with invalid second factor
test_cases.preconditions: A registered company representative account exists configured to use two separate factors (e.g., password and SMS OTP).
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid username, valid password, invalid SMS OTP.

steps.action: Enter the valid username and password for the company representative.
steps.expected: The system sends an OTP and prompts for it.

steps.action: Enter an invalid OTP.
steps.expected: The system rejects the authentication attempt and displays an error message.

test_cases.title: Inactivity timeout triggers reauthentication for AAL2 session
test_cases.preconditions: A citizen or company representative is logged in with an active AAL2 session. The inactivity timeout value is defined in VBP SDD §14.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid AAL2 credentials.
test_cases.assumptions: The inactivity timeout duration is set to a testable value (e.g., 5 minutes) in the test environment configuration.

steps.action: Log in with valid AAL2 credentials to establish a session.
steps.expected: The user is authenticated and the session is active.

steps.action: Wait for the defined inactivity timeout period without performing any actions.
steps.expected: The session remains active but is flagged as inactive.

steps.action: Perform an action that requires session validation (e.g., navigate to a protected page).
steps.expected: The system prompts for reauthentication (e.g., password or MFA) as per NIST SP 800-63B-4 §5.2.

steps.action: Provide valid reauthentication credentials.
steps.expected: The session is re-authenticated and the user continues without interruption.

test_cases.title: Overall timeout terminates AAL2 session
test_cases.preconditions: A citizen or company representative is logged in with an active AAL2 session. The overall timeout value is defined in VBP SDD §14.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid AAL2 credentials.
test_cases.assumptions: The overall timeout duration is set to a testable value (e.g., 30 minutes) in the test environment configuration.

steps.action: Log in with valid AAL2 credentials to establish a session.
steps.expected: The user is authenticated and the session is active.

steps.action: Wait for the defined overall timeout period, performing periodic actions to prevent inactivity timeout.
steps.expected: The session remains active during the wait period.

steps.action: Perform an action after the overall timeout has elapsed.
steps.expected: The session is terminated, and the user is redirected to the login page.

test_cases.title: Reauthentication failure during inactivity timeout
test_cases.preconditions: A citizen or company representative is logged in with an active AAL2 session. The inactivity timeout has been reached.
test_cases.test_inputs: Invalid reauthentication credentials.
test_cases.assumptions: The inactivity timeout duration is set to a testable value in the test environment configuration.

steps.action: Wait for the inactivity timeout to elapse.
steps.expected: The session is flagged as inactive.

steps.action: Perform an action that triggers reauthentication.
steps.expected: The system prompts for reauthentication.

steps.action: Provide invalid reauthentication credentials.
steps.expected: The reauthentication fails, and the session is terminated or locked as per security policy.

test_cases.title: Notification sent to representative upon account recovery
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists and is in a recoverable state (e.g., locked or password reset initiated).
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid recovery credentials for the representative account.
test_cases.assumptions: The notification channel (e.g., email) is configured and monitored for the representative.

steps.action: Initiate the account recovery process for the company representative account using valid recovery credentials.
steps.expected: The system successfully processes the recovery request.

steps.action: Check the notification channel (e.g., email inbox) associated with the representative.
steps.expected: A notification message regarding the account recovery is received by the representative.

test_cases.title: Notification sent to designee upon account recovery
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with a designated alternate contact (designee) configured for notifications.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid recovery credentials for the representative account.
test_cases.assumptions: The designee's notification channel is configured and monitored.

steps.action: Initiate the account recovery process for the company representative account using valid recovery credentials.
steps.expected: The system successfully processes the recovery request.

steps.action: Check the notification channel associated with the designee.
steps.expected: A notification message regarding the account recovery is received by the designee.

test_cases.title: Account notification sent to registered email address
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with a valid email address registered as a notification address.
test_cases.test_inputs: Trigger event for account notification (e.g., password change or login alert).
test_cases.assumptions: The email server is configured and reachable for test purposes.

steps.action: Trigger an account notification event for the company representative account.
steps.expected: The system generates a notification message.

steps.action: Check the inbox of the registered email address.
steps.expected: The notification email is received with the correct content.

test_cases.title: Account notification sent to registered phone number
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with a valid phone number registered as a notification address.
test_cases.test_inputs: Trigger event for account notification.
test_cases.assumptions: SMS gateway is configured and reachable for test purposes.

steps.action: Trigger an account notification event for the company representative account.
steps.expected: The system generates a notification message.

steps.action: Check the device associated with the registered phone number.
steps.expected: The notification SMS is received with the correct content.

test_cases.title: No notification sent to postal address
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with only a postal address registered as a notification address.
test_cases.test_inputs: Trigger event for account notification.

steps.action: Trigger an account notification event for the company representative account.
steps.expected: The system processes the notification request.

steps.action: Verify that no digital notification (email/SMS) is sent.
steps.expected: No email or SMS is sent to any address, as postal addresses are excluded from digital notifications.

test_cases.title: Notification sent to all registered digital addresses
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with multiple registered notification addresses: one email and one phone number.
test_cases.test_inputs: Trigger event for account notification.
test_cases.assumptions: Email and SMS services are available.

steps.action: Trigger an account notification event for the company representative account.
steps.expected: The system generates notification messages for all registered digital addresses.

steps.action: Check the inbox of the registered email address.
steps.expected: The notification email is received.

steps.action: Check the device associated with the registered phone number.
steps.expected: The notification SMS is received.

test_cases.title: VBP oturumunun e-Devlet assertion geçerlilik süresinden bağımsızlığı
test_cases.preconditions: Kullanıcının e-Devlet üzerinden başarılı bir kimlik doğrulaması yapılmış ve VBP oturumu başlatılmıştır. VBP oturum süresi, e-Devlet assertion geçerlilik süresinden uzundur.
test_cases.test_inputs: Geçerli e-Devlet assertion'ı içeren bir oturum.
test_cases.assumptions: VBP oturum süresi, e-Devlet assertion geçerlilik süresinden en az 10 dakika uzundur.

steps.action: e-Devlet assertion geçerlilik süresinin dolmasını bekleyin.
steps.expected: VBP oturumu devam eder, kullanıcı oturumdan atılmaz.

steps.action: VBP'de bir sayfa yenileyin veya yeni bir sayfa açın.
steps.expected: Sayfa başarıyla yüklenir, kullanıcı oturumda kalır.

test_cases.title: Federation transaction initiation includes VBP identifier and nonce
test_cases.preconditions: VBP is configured with a valid identifier for e-Devlet federation. A valid user session is established in VBP.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid user credentials for VBP.
test_cases.assumptions: The e-Devlet endpoint is available and the network connection is stable. The VBP system is configured to log or expose the outgoing assertion request for verification purposes.

steps.action: Initiate a federation transaction from VBP to e-Devlet using a valid user session.
steps.expected: The system generates an assertion request to e-Devlet.

steps.action: Inspect the content of the generated assertion request.
steps.expected: The request contains a field identifying VBP (VBP identifier) and a field containing a cryptographic nonce.

test_cases.title: Cryptographic nonce is unique per transaction
test_cases.preconditions: VBP is configured for federation with e-Devlet. A valid user session is established.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid user credentials for VBP.
test_cases.assumptions: The system allows multiple consecutive federation transactions for testing purposes.

steps.action: Initiate the first federation transaction and record the cryptographic nonce from the assertion request.
steps.expected: A nonce value N1 is present in the request.

steps.action: Initiate a second federation transaction and record the cryptographic nonce from the assertion request.
steps.expected: A nonce value N2 is present in the request.

steps.action: Compare nonce N1 and nonce N2.
steps.expected: N1 and N2 are different values, indicating the nonce is unique per transaction.

test_cases.title: VBP audience identifier'ı içeren e-Devlet assertion'ının kabul edilmesi
test_cases.preconditions: VBP, e-Devlet SSO ile entegre edilmiş ve test ortamında çalışmaktadır.
test_cases.test_inputs: Audience alanı VBP'nin tanımlayıcısını içeren geçerli bir e-Devlet assertion'ı.
test_cases.assumptions: VBP'nin e-Devlet'te kayıtlı benzersiz tanımlayıcısı (client_id veya benzeri) test ortamında bilinen bir değerdir.

steps.action: Audience alanı VBP'nin tanımlayıcısını içeren geçerli bir e-Devlet assertion'ı VBP'ye gönderilir.
steps.expected: VBP assertion'ı doğrular ve kullanıcı oturumunu başarıyla başlatır.

test_cases.title: VBP audience identifier'ı içermeyen e-Devlet assertion'ının reddedilmesi
test_cases.preconditions: VBP, e-Devlet SSO ile entegre edilmiş ve test ortamında çalışmaktadır.
test_cases.test_inputs: Audience alanı başka bir RP'nin tanımlayıcısını içeren geçerli bir e-Devlet assertion'ı.
test_cases.assumptions: Başka bir RP'nin e-Devlet'te kayıtlı benzersiz tanımlayıcısı test ortamında bilinen bir değerdir.

steps.action: Audience alanı başka bir RP'nin tanımlayıcısını içeren geçerli bir e-Devlet assertion'ı VBP'ye gönderilir.
steps.expected: VBP assertion'ı reddeder ve kullanıcı oturumu başlatılmaz. Hata mesajı veya yönlendirme yapılır.

test_cases.title: Audience alanı boş olan e-Devlet assertion'ının reddedilmesi
test_cases.preconditions: VBP, e-Devlet SSO ile entegre edilmiş ve test ortamında çalışmaktadır.
test_cases.test_inputs: Audience alanı boş veya eksik olan bir e-Devlet assertion'ı.

steps.action: Audience alanı boş veya eksik olan bir e-Devlet assertion'ı VBP'ye gönderilir.
steps.expected: VBP assertion'ı reddeder ve kullanıcı oturumu başlatılmaz.

test_cases.title: Setting a new phone number triggers authenticator binding process
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with a pre-registered telephone number. The user is authenticated.
test_cases.test_inputs: A new valid telephone number.
test_cases.assumptions: The system implements the NIST SP 800-63B-4 §4.1.2 binding process, which typically involves sending a one-time code to the new number and verifying it.

steps.action: Navigate to the profile settings and select the option to change the pre-registered telephone number.
steps.expected: The system initiates the authenticator binding process (e.g., prompts for a new number and sends a verification code to the new number) rather than simply saving the number.

steps.action: Enter the new telephone number and submit the form.
steps.expected: The system sends a one-time code to the new telephone number and waits for verification.

steps.action: Enter the correct one-time code received on the new telephone number.
steps.expected: The system verifies the code, completes the binding process, and updates the pre-registered telephone number to the new one.

test_cases.title: Changing phone number without verification fails
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with a pre-registered telephone number. The user is authenticated.
test_cases.test_inputs: A new valid telephone number, an incorrect one-time code.
test_cases.assumptions: The binding process requires successful verification of a code sent to the new number.

steps.action: Initiate the change of the pre-registered telephone number to a new number.
steps.expected: The system sends a one-time code to the new telephone number.

steps.action: Enter an incorrect one-time code.
steps.expected: The system rejects the code, displays an error message, and does not update the pre-registered telephone number.

steps.action: Check the current pre-registered telephone number in the profile.
steps.expected: The original pre-registered telephone number remains unchanged.

test_cases.title: Setting phone number for a new representative triggers binding
test_cases.preconditions: A new company representative account is being created or updated. The user is authenticated.
test_cases.test_inputs: A valid telephone number.
test_cases.assumptions: The 'setting' of a pre-registered number for a representative is treated as binding a new authenticator.

steps.action: Provide a telephone number for the company representative during the registration or profile setup.
steps.expected: The system treats this as an authenticator binding event and initiates the verification process (e.g., sends a code to the provided number).

steps.action: Verify the code sent to the telephone number.
steps.expected: The telephone number is successfully bound as the pre-registered authenticator for the representative.

test_cases.title: Binding a second authenticator to a company representative account
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with one active authenticator bound.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid credentials for the company representative account; a new authenticator device or secret.
test_cases.assumptions: The system supports at least two authenticators per account as per NIST SP 800-63B-4 §4.1.2.1.

steps.action: Log in to the company representative account using the existing authenticator.
steps.expected: The user is successfully authenticated and redirected to the account management or security settings page.

steps.action: Initiate the process to add a new authenticator.
steps.expected: The system displays a prompt or interface to register a new authenticator (e.g., QR code, secret key, or device pairing).

steps.action: Complete the registration of the new authenticator by providing the required verification code or pairing data.
steps.expected: The system confirms the successful binding of the new authenticator to the account.

steps.action: View the list of bound authenticators for the account.
steps.expected: Both the original and the newly added authenticator are listed as active.

test_cases.title: Binding a third authenticator to a company representative account
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with two active authenticators bound.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid credentials for the company representative account; a third new authenticator device or secret.
test_cases.assumptions: The system allows more than two authenticators per account as per NIST SP 800-63B-4 §4.1.2.1.

steps.action: Log in to the company representative account using one of the existing authenticators.
steps.expected: The user is successfully authenticated.

steps.action: Initiate the process to add a third authenticator.
steps.expected: The system allows the initiation of the new authenticator registration process.

steps.action: Complete the registration of the third authenticator.
steps.expected: The system confirms the successful binding of the third authenticator.

steps.action: View the list of bound authenticators for the account.
steps.expected: All three authenticators are listed as active.

test_cases.title: Attempting to bind an authenticator to a non-representative account
test_cases.preconditions: A standard user account (not a company representative) exists.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid credentials for the standard user account.
test_cases.assumptions: The requirement specifically applies to company representative accounts; other account types may have different rules or restrictions.

steps.action: Log in to the standard user account.
steps.expected: The user is successfully authenticated.

steps.action: Attempt to access the multi-authenticator binding feature if available in the UI, or attempt to add a second authenticator.
steps.expected: The system either hides the option to add multiple authenticators or rejects the request with an error message indicating that this feature is not available for this account type.

test_cases.title: Authentication required at lower AAL when account max is lower than authenticator max
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with a maximum available AAL of 2. A new authenticator capable of AAL 3 is ready to be bound.
test_cases.test_inputs: Account with max AAL 2, New authenticator with max AAL 3
test_cases.assumptions: The system supports AAL levels 1, 2, and 3 as defined in NIST SP 800-63B-4.

steps.action: Initiate the process to bind the new authenticator to the account.
steps.expected: The system prompts for authentication.

steps.action: Provide authentication credentials corresponding to AAL 2.
steps.expected: The authentication is accepted, and the new authenticator is successfully bound to the account.

test_cases.title: Authentication required at lower AAL when authenticator max is lower than account max
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with a maximum available AAL of 3. A new authenticator capable of AAL 1 is ready to be bound.
test_cases.test_inputs: Account with max AAL 3, New authenticator with max AAL 1
test_cases.assumptions: The system supports AAL levels 1, 2, and 3 as defined in NIST SP 800-63B-4.

steps.action: Initiate the process to bind the new authenticator to the account.
steps.expected: The system prompts for authentication.

steps.action: Provide authentication credentials corresponding to AAL 1.
steps.expected: The authentication is accepted, and the new authenticator is successfully bound to the account.

test_cases.title: Authentication required at AAL 2 when both account and authenticator support AAL 2
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with a maximum available AAL of 2. A new authenticator capable of AAL 2 is ready to be bound.
test_cases.test_inputs: Account with max AAL 2, New authenticator with max AAL 2
test_cases.assumptions: The system supports AAL levels 1, 2, and 3 as defined in NIST SP 800-63B-4.

steps.action: Initiate the process to bind the new authenticator to the account.
steps.expected: The system prompts for authentication.

steps.action: Provide authentication credentials corresponding to AAL 2.
steps.expected: The authentication is accepted, and the new authenticator is successfully bound to the account.

test_cases.title: Authentication at lower AAL is rejected when higher AAL is required
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with a maximum available AAL of 3. A new authenticator capable of AAL 3 is ready to be bound.
test_cases.test_inputs: Account with max AAL 3, New authenticator with max AAL 3
test_cases.assumptions: The system supports AAL levels 1, 2, and 3 as defined in NIST SP 800-63B-4.

steps.action: Initiate the process to bind the new authenticator to the account.
steps.expected: The system prompts for authentication.

steps.action: Provide authentication credentials corresponding to AAL 1.
steps.expected: The authentication is rejected, and an error message indicating insufficient assurance level is displayed.

test_cases.title: Notification sent via independent channel upon authenticator addition
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with a valid email address registered. The account is not currently locked.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid credentials for the company representative account. A new authenticator device (e.g., TOTP app or hardware key) ready for enrollment.
test_cases.assumptions: The 'independent mechanism' is assumed to be email, as it is the standard out-of-band channel distinct from the in-band transaction of adding the authenticator. The email server is operational.

steps.action: Log in to the VBP portal using the company representative account credentials.
steps.expected: The user is successfully authenticated and redirected to the dashboard or security settings page.

steps.action: Navigate to the security settings and initiate the process to add a new authenticator.
steps.expected: The system displays the enrollment interface (e.g., QR code or setup key) for the new authenticator.

steps.action: Complete the enrollment process by confirming the new authenticator on the device and submitting the confirmation in the portal.
steps.expected: The system confirms the successful addition of the authenticator to the account.

steps.action: Check the email inbox associated with the account for a notification message.
steps.expected: An email notification is received indicating that a new authenticator has been added to the account. The email is sent from a system address and does not require interaction with the current browser session to be delivered.

test_cases.title: Notification content includes account identifier and timestamp
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with a valid email address. A new authenticator is added to the account.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid credentials. New authenticator device.
test_cases.assumptions: The notification email contains standard security event details as per NIST SP 800-63B-4 recommendations for out-of-band notifications.

steps.action: Add a new authenticator to the company representative account and complete the enrollment.
steps.expected: The authenticator is successfully bound to the account.

steps.action: Open the notification email received in the account's email inbox.
steps.expected: The email body contains the account identifier (e.g., username or masked email) and the timestamp of the event, allowing the user to verify the legitimacy of the change.

test_cases.title: No notification sent if authenticator addition fails
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists. The email inbox is monitored.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid credentials. An invalid or expired TOTP code for enrollment confirmation.
test_cases.assumptions: The system only sends the notification upon successful binding of the authenticator.

steps.action: Initiate the process to add a new authenticator.
steps.expected: The enrollment interface is displayed.

steps.action: Enter an incorrect or expired verification code to confirm the new authenticator.
steps.expected: The system rejects the enrollment and displays an error message. The authenticator is not added to the account.

steps.action: Check the email inbox for a notification regarding the authenticator addition.
steps.expected: No notification email is received, as the transaction was not successful.

test_cases.title: E-posta onay kodunun başarılı kullanımdan sonra geçersiz kılınması
test_cases.preconditions: Kayıt sürecinde şirket temsilcisi için e-posta onay kodu gönderilmiştir ve kod henüz kullanılmamıştır.
test_cases.test_inputs: Geçerli onay kodu.

steps.action: Gönderilen onay kodu sistemde doğrulanmak üzere gönderilir.
steps.expected: Kod doğrulanır ve e-posta adresi onaylanır.

steps.action: Aynı onay kodu, geçerlilik süresi (60 dakika) dolmadan ikinci kez gönderilir.
steps.expected: Kod reddedilir ve 'kod geçersiz' veya benzeri bir hata mesajı gösterilir.

test_cases.title: SMS kodunun 5 dakikalık geçerlilik süresi içinde doğrulanması
test_cases.preconditions: Şirket temsilcisi birinci faktörü (parola) başarıyla girmiştir ve SMS kodu gönderilmiştir.
test_cases.test_inputs: Doğru SMS kodu.
test_cases.assumptions: Kod gönderiminden itibaren 5 dakikadan kısa bir süre geçmiştir.

steps.action: SMS kodu, gönderimden 1 dakika sonra sistemde doğrulanmak üzere gönderilir.
steps.expected: Kod kabul edilir ve ikinci faktör doğrulaması tamamlanır, kullanıcı oturum açar.

test_cases.title: SMS kodunun 5 dakikalık geçerlilik süresi aşıldığında reddedilmesi
test_cases.preconditions: Şirket temsilcisi birinci faktörü (parola) başarıyla girmiştir ve SMS kodu gönderilmiştir.
test_cases.test_inputs: Doğru SMS kodu.
test_cases.assumptions: Kod gönderiminden itibaren 5 dakikadan fazla bir süre geçmiştir.

steps.action: SMS kodu, gönderimden 5 dakika 1 saniye sonra sistemde doğrulanmak üzere gönderilir.
steps.expected: Kod reddedilir, kullanıcı oturum açamaz ve hata mesajı gösterilir.

test_cases.title: 15 karakterden kısa parolanın reddedilmesi
test_cases.preconditions: Şirket temsilcisi hesap aktivasyonu veya parola değiştirme ekranındadır.
test_cases.test_inputs: 14 karakter uzunluğunda bir parola.

steps.action: 14 karakter uzunluğundaki parola gönderilir.

test_cases.title: VBP'nin e-Devlet ile federasyon işleminde RP rolüyle başlatması

test_cases.title: e-Devlet'in RP rolüyle VBP'ye istek gönderememesi (Yön Doğruluğu)

steps.expected: VBP bu isteği reddeder veya yok sayar. VBP, e-Devlet'e IdP olarak yanıt vermez. Sistem loglarında 'Beklenmeyen istek kaynağı' veya 'RP rolü ihlali' gibi bir hata kaydı oluşur.

test_cases.title: Başarısız doğrulama sonrası hata mesajının belirsiz olması

test_cases.title: Başarılı ve başarısız doğrulama yanıt sürelerinin benzerliği

steps.action: Yetkili kaynakta kaydı olmayan vatandaş bilgileriyle doğrulama istemi gönderilir ve yanıt süresi ölçülür.
steps.expected: Sistem başarısız doğrulama yanıtını döndürür. Yanıt süresi kaydedilir.

steps.action: İki senaryodaki yanıt süreleri karşılaştırılır.
steps.expected: Başarılı ve başarısız senaryolar arasındaki yanıt süresi farkı, saldırganın sonucu tahmin etmesine izin verecek kadar belirgin değildir (örneğin, sabit gecikme süresi uygulanmıştır).

test_cases.title: IAL2 Company Representative Proofing via Authoritative Source Comparison
test_cases.preconditions: A test user account is created with IAL2 assurance level. The user is identified as a company representative. The system is connected to a mock authoritative source (e.g., MERSIS or similar) containing valid core attributes for this representative.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid government identifier (e.g., TC Kimlik No), valid company registration number, and other core attributes matching the authoritative source.
test_cases.assumptions: The authoritative source returns a positive match for the provided attributes.

steps.action: Initiate the proofing process for the company representative user with IAL2 level.
steps.expected: The system prompts for core attributes including government identifier and company details.

steps.action: Submit the valid government identifier and core attributes that match the authoritative source.
steps.expected: The system validates the attributes against the authoritative source and returns a success status.

steps.action: Check the user's assurance level status in the system.
steps.expected: The user's IAL2 proofing status is marked as 'Verified' or 'Validated'.

test_cases.title: IAL2 Company Representative Proofing via Digital Signature Validation
test_cases.preconditions: A test user account is created with IAL2 assurance level. The user is identified as a company representative. A digitally signed evidence document (SUPERIOR evidence) is prepared with a valid issuer public key.
test_cases.test_inputs: A digitally signed PDF or data object containing core attributes, signed by a trusted issuer. The issuer's public key is available in the system's trust store.
test_cases.assumptions: The digital signature is cryptographically valid and the issuer is recognized by the system.

steps.action: Initiate the proofing process for the company representative user with IAL2 level.
steps.expected: The system allows the upload or submission of digitally signed evidence.

steps.action: Submit the digitally signed evidence document containing the core attributes.
steps.expected: The system validates the digital signature using the issuer's public key and extracts the core attributes.

steps.action: Check the user's assurance level status in the system.
steps.expected: The user's IAL2 proofing status is marked as 'Verified' or 'Validated' based on the successful signature validation.

test_cases.title: IAL2 Proofing Failure Due to Mismatched Attributes in Authoritative Source
test_cases.preconditions: A test user account is created with IAL2 assurance level. The user is identified as a company representative. The authoritative source contains different values for the core attributes than those submitted.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid government identifier, but a company registration number that does not match the authoritative source.
test_cases.assumptions: The authoritative source returns a negative match or no match for the provided attributes.

steps.action: Initiate the proofing process for the company representative user with IAL2 level.
steps.expected: The system prompts for core attributes.

steps.action: Submit the government identifier and core attributes that do not match the authoritative source.
steps.expected: The system fails the validation and returns an error message indicating a mismatch.

steps.action: Check the user's assurance level status in the system.
steps.expected: The user's IAL2 proofing status remains 'Unverified' or is marked as 'Failed'.

test_cases.title: IAL2 Proofing Failure Due to Invalid Digital Signature
test_cases.preconditions: A test user account is created with IAL2 assurance level. The user is identified as a company representative. A digitally signed evidence document is prepared with an invalid or tampered signature.
test_cases.test_inputs: A digitally signed evidence document where the signature is invalid (e.g., tampered content or unknown issuer key).
test_cases.assumptions: The system detects the invalid signature during validation.

steps.action: Initiate the proofing process for the company representative user with IAL2 level.
steps.expected: The system allows the upload or submission of digitally signed evidence.

steps.action: Submit the digitally signed evidence document with an invalid signature.
steps.expected: The system fails the signature validation and returns an error message indicating an invalid signature.

steps.action: Check the user's assurance level status in the system.
steps.expected: The user's IAL2 proofing status remains 'Unverified' or is marked as 'Failed'.

test_cases.title: IAL2 Proofing with Missing Core Attributes
test_cases.preconditions: A test user account is created with IAL2 assurance level. The user is identified as a company representative.
test_cases.test_inputs: Input data missing one or more required core attributes (e.g., missing government identifier).
test_cases.assumptions: The system enforces the presence of all core attributes for IAL2 validation.

steps.action: Initiate the proofing process for the company representative user with IAL2 level.
steps.expected: The system prompts for core attributes.

steps.action: Submit input data with missing core attributes.
steps.expected: The system rejects the submission and displays an error message indicating missing required fields.

steps.action: Check the user's assurance level status in the system.
steps.expected: The user's IAL2 proofing status remains 'Unverified'.

test_cases.title: IAL2 kimlik doğrulama sonrası bildirim gönderimi
test_cases.preconditions: Sistemde doğrulanmış bir şirket temsilcisi hesabı ve geçerli bir e-posta adresi tanımlıdır.
test_cases.test_inputs: Doğrulanmış e-posta adresi, IAL2 kimlik doğrulama süreci için gerekli tüm geçerli belgeler ve bilgiler.

test_cases.test_inputs: One valid recovery code and a valid TOTP code from the bound authenticator.
test_cases.assumptions: The account has a registered single-factor authenticator bound to it.

steps.action: Initiate the account recovery process.
steps.expected: The system presents recovery options, including 'Recovery code + Authenticator'.

steps.action: Select the option to recover using a recovery code and authenticator.
steps.expected: The system prompts for the recovery code.

steps.action: Enter the valid recovery code.
steps.expected: The system accepts the code and prompts for the authenticator code.

steps.action: Enter the current valid code from the bound single-factor authenticator.
steps.expected: The system verifies the authenticator code and successfully recovers the account.

test_cases.title: Recovery via repeated identity proofing
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account with AAL2 authentication is in recovery mode. The user has access to identity documents required for proofing.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid identity document data (e.g., ID number, name, date of birth) matching the account records.
test_cases.assumptions: The system has a defined identity proofing workflow compliant with NIST SP 800-63B-4 §4.2.2.2.

steps.action: Initiate the account recovery process.
steps.expected: The system presents recovery options, including 'Identity Proofing'.

steps.action: Select the option to recover via identity proofing.
steps.expected: The system initiates the identity proofing workflow, requesting identity details.

steps.action: Provide the required identity information (e.g., full name, ID number).
steps.expected: The system validates the information against the stored records.

steps.action: Complete any additional verification steps required by the proofing workflow (e.g., answering security questions or document upload if part of the flow).
steps.expected: The system confirms the identity and successfully recovers the account.

test_cases.title: Recovery failure with two codes from the same method
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is in recovery mode. Two valid recovery codes generated via the same method (e.g., both via SMS) are available.
test_cases.test_inputs: Two valid recovery codes from the same channel (SMS).
test_cases.assumptions: The system can distinguish the source method of each recovery code.

steps.action: Select the option to recover using two recovery codes.
steps.expected: The system prompts for the first recovery code.

steps.action: Enter the first valid recovery code obtained via SMS.
steps.expected: The system accepts the first code and prompts for the second.

steps.action: Enter the second valid recovery code also obtained via SMS.
steps.expected: The system rejects the recovery attempt, indicating that the codes must be from different methods.

test_cases.title: Recovery failure with invalid recovery code
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is in recovery mode.
test_cases.test_inputs: An invalid or expired recovery code.

steps.action: Select the option to recover using a recovery code and authenticator.
steps.expected: The system prompts for the recovery code.

steps.action: Enter an invalid recovery code.
steps.expected: The system rejects the code and displays an error message, preventing progression to the authenticator step.

test_cases.title: Recovery failure with unbound authenticator
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is in recovery mode. The user has a valid recovery code but the authenticator used is not bound to the account.
test_cases.test_inputs: One valid recovery code and a TOTP code from an unbound authenticator.
test_cases.assumptions: The system can verify if an authenticator is bound to the specific account.

steps.action: Select the option to recover using a recovery code and authenticator.
steps.expected: The system prompts for the recovery code.

steps.action: Enter the valid recovery code.
steps.expected: The system accepts the code and prompts for the authenticator code.

steps.action: Enter a valid TOTP code from an authenticator not bound to the account.
steps.expected: The system rejects the authenticator code, indicating it is not associated with the account, and fails the recovery attempt.

test_cases.title: Disabling multiple authenticators after threshold reached
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with password and a second factor (e.g., TOTP) enabled. The account is not currently locked or disabled.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid username, incorrect password, incorrect second factor code.
test_cases.assumptions: The threshold for failed attempts defined in VBP Software Design Document §14 is 5 consecutive failures.

steps.action: Attempt login with the valid username, an incorrect password, and an incorrect second factor code.
steps.expected: Authentication fails. The system records the failure for both the password and the second factor authenticators.

steps.action: Repeat the failed login attempt with incorrect password and incorrect second factor code until the threshold (5 attempts) is reached.
steps.expected: After the 5th consecutive failure, the system disables both the password authenticator and the second factor authenticator for the account.

steps.action: Attempt login again with the correct password and correct second factor code.
steps.expected: Authentication is rejected because the authenticators are disabled. The user is informed that the account requires administrative intervention or reset.

test_cases.title: No disabling when threshold is not reached
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with password and a second factor enabled. The account is not currently locked or disabled.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid username, incorrect password, incorrect second factor code.
test_cases.assumptions: The threshold for failed attempts defined in VBP Software Design Document §14 is 5 consecutive failures.

steps.action: Attempt login with the valid username, an incorrect password, and an incorrect second factor code 4 times consecutively.
steps.expected: Authentication fails each time. The system records the failures but does not disable any authenticators.

steps.action: Attempt login with the correct password and correct second factor code.
steps.expected: Authentication succeeds. The user logs in successfully, confirming that the authenticators remain active.

test_cases.title: Disabling only involved authenticators when one factor is correct
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with password and a second factor enabled. The account is not currently locked or disabled.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid username, incorrect password, correct second factor code.
test_cases.assumptions: The threshold for failed attempts defined in VBP Software Design Document §14 is 5 consecutive failures. The system tracks failures per authenticator involved in the failed attempt.

steps.action: Attempt login with the valid username, an incorrect password, and a correct second factor code 5 times consecutively.
steps.expected: Authentication fails each time due to the incorrect password. The system records failures for the password authenticator. The second factor authenticator is not involved in the failure (as it was correct) and should not be disabled if the logic strictly disables only 'involved' failed authenticators. However, if the requirement implies disabling all authenticators on the account upon reaching the threshold for the account, both may be disabled. Based on 'disable all of the authenticators involved', only the password should be disabled if the second factor was correct. Let's assume the system disables the specific authenticator that failed. If the requirement means 'all authenticators on the account', the test expectation changes. Given 'involved in consecutive failed authentication attempts', it implies the ones that were part of the failed attempt. If the second factor was correct, it wasn't the cause of failure, but it was 'involved' in the attempt. NIST 800-63B-4 §3.2.2 typically suggests locking the account or disabling the specific factor. Let's stick to the literal interpretation: 'disable all of the authenticators involved'. If the second factor was correct, it was involved in the attempt. So both might be disabled. Let's refine the test to be clearer: Use incorrect password and incorrect second factor to ensure both are 'involved' in the failure. The previous test TC-038-01 covers this. This test case is ambiguous if one factor is correct. Let's change this test case to verify that if the threshold is reached, the account is locked/disabled such that no login is possible, regardless of which specific factor failed, to ensure security. Actually, the requirement says 'disable all of the authenticators involved'. If I enter wrong password and right OTP, the password is involved in the failure. The OTP is involved in the attempt but not the failure. Let's assume 'involved' means 'used in the failed attempt'. So both are disabled. Let's test that.

steps.action: Attempt login with the correct password and correct second factor code.
steps.expected: Authentication is rejected because the authenticators are disabled.

test_cases.title: Rebinding a disabled authenticator to the company representative account
test_cases.preconditions: An authenticator has been disabled due to reaching the failed-attempt threshold defined in VBP SDD §14. A valid company representative account exists.
test_cases.test_inputs: Credentials for the company representative account and the disabled authenticator.
test_cases.assumptions: The failed-attempt threshold is defined in the VBP Software Design Document §14. The rebinding process follows NIST SP 800-63B-4 §4.1 and VBP SDD §3.2.2.

steps.action: Attempt to use the disabled authenticator for authentication without rebinding it.
steps.expected: The system rejects the authentication attempt and indicates that the authenticator is disabled.

steps.action: Initiate the rebinding process for the disabled authenticator to the company representative account as specified in §3.2.2.
steps.expected: The system accepts the rebinding request and associates the authenticator with the company representative account.

steps.action: Attempt to use the rebound authenticator for authentication.
steps.expected: The system accepts the authenticator and allows the authentication to proceed.

test_cases.title: Rebinding a disabled authenticator to an incorrect account
test_cases.preconditions: An authenticator has been disabled due to reaching the failed-attempt threshold. A valid company representative account and a different user account exist.
test_cases.test_inputs: Credentials for the different user account and the disabled authenticator.
test_cases.assumptions: The system enforces that the authenticator must be bound to the specific company representative account as per §3.2.2.

steps.action: Initiate the rebinding process for the disabled authenticator to a non-company representative account.
steps.expected: The system rejects the rebinding request and indicates that the authenticator must be bound to the company representative account.

steps.action: Attempt to use the authenticator for authentication.
steps.expected: The system rejects the authentication attempt as the authenticator remains disabled.

test_cases.title: Request handling when e-Devlet response fails IAL requirement
test_cases.preconditions: VBP is configured to require a specific IAL level for the service. A mock e-Devlet service is available to return a response with a lower IAL level than required.
test_cases.test_inputs: A valid citizen session with an e-Devlet response indicating an IAL level lower than the VBP requirement.
test_cases.assumptions: The 'defined mechanism' for handling insufficient IAL is configured to decline the request and display a specific error message.

steps.action: Initiate a request for a service that requires a specific IAL level.
steps.expected: The request is sent to the e-Devlet service.

steps.action: The mock e-Devlet service returns a response with an IAL level lower than the VBP requirement.
steps.expected: VBP detects the IAL mismatch.

steps.action: Observe the VBP response to the citizen.
steps.expected: The request is declined, and the citizen is informed that the authentication level is insufficient, as per the defined mechanism.

test_cases.title: Session AAL cannot exceed authentication event AAL
test_cases.preconditions: A user account exists with AAL1 authentication capability. The system allows session configuration or API calls to set session AAL.
test_cases.test_inputs: User credentials for AAL1 login. Request to set session AAL to AAL2.
test_cases.assumptions: The system exposes a mechanism (API or configuration) to attempt setting a session's AAL higher than the authentication event's AAL.

steps.action: Authenticate the user using AAL1 methods (e.g., password only).
steps.expected: Authentication succeeds and a session is created with AAL1.

steps.action: Attempt to upgrade the current session to AAL2 without performing a new AAL2 authentication event.
steps.expected: The system rejects the request or ignores the upgrade, keeping the session at AAL1. The session is not treated as AAL2.

test_cases.title: Session AAL can be lower than authentication event AAL
test_cases.preconditions: A user account exists with AAL2 authentication capability (e.g., password + OTP).
test_cases.test_inputs: User credentials for AAL2 login. Request to set session AAL to AAL1.
test_cases.assumptions: The system allows downgrading the session AAL to a lower level than the authentication event.

steps.action: Authenticate the user using AAL2 methods.
steps.expected: Authentication succeeds and a session is created with AAL2.

steps.action: Configure or request the session to operate at AAL1.
steps.expected: The system accepts the configuration. The session is treated as AAL1 for subsequent access control decisions.

test_cases.title: Authenticated session remains on HTTPS after navigation
test_cases.preconditions: A valid user account exists. The browser is configured to allow both HTTP and HTTPS connections.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid credentials for authentication.
test_cases.assumptions: The portal supports standard browser navigation and URL manipulation for testing purposes.

steps.action: Navigate to the portal login page via HTTPS and log in with valid credentials.
steps.expected: The user is successfully authenticated and redirected to the dashboard or home page over HTTPS.

steps.action: While authenticated, manually change the URL scheme from 'https' to 'http' in the browser address bar and press Enter.
steps.expected: The browser is redirected back to the HTTPS version of the page, or the request is rejected, ensuring the session does not continue over insecure HTTP.

steps.action: Verify the current URL scheme in the browser address bar.
steps.expected: The URL scheme is 'https'.

test_cases.title: Prevention of downgrade via mixed content or forced HTTP request
test_cases.preconditions: User is authenticated via HTTPS.
test_cases.test_inputs: A valid session cookie/token.
test_cases.assumptions: Network traffic can be intercepted or modified using a proxy tool (e.g., Burp Suite) to simulate a downgrade attempt.

steps.action: Log in to the portal via HTTPS.
steps.expected: Authentication is successful.

steps.action: Using a proxy tool, intercept the next request and modify the destination URL from HTTPS to HTTP while keeping the session credentials intact.
steps.expected: The server rejects the request or redirects it to HTTPS. The session is not established or continued over the insecure HTTP connection.

steps.action: Check the response status and headers.
steps.expected: The response indicates a redirect to HTTPS (301/302) or an error, and no sensitive data is transmitted over HTTP.

test_cases.title: Bot detection blocks automated identity proofing attempts
test_cases.preconditions: The VBP identity proofing endpoint is accessible. A headless browser or automated script is configured to mimic a user agent.
test_cases.test_inputs: Automated script simulating a user agent with missing or inconsistent browser fingerprint headers.
test_cases.assumptions: The system's bot detection mechanism is active and configured to block non-human traffic.

steps.action: Initiate an identity proofing request using an automated script that lacks standard browser fingerprinting characteristics (e.g., missing WebGL or Canvas data).
steps.expected: The request is rejected or challenged by the bot detection mechanism. The user is not allowed to proceed to the next step of the identity proofing process.

steps.action: Check the server logs or security dashboard for the blocked request.
steps.expected: The event is logged as a potential bot attack or automated access attempt, and the IP address or session is flagged.

test_cases.title: Web Application Firewall blocks malicious input in identity proofing forms
test_cases.preconditions: The VBP identity proofing form is accessible. The WAF is configured to block common SQL injection and XSS patterns.
test_cases.test_inputs: A form field containing a SQL injection payload (e.g., ' OR 1=1 --) and a script tag payload (<script>alert(1)</script>).
test_cases.assumptions: The WAF rules are active and configured to inspect POST/GET parameters for the identity proofing endpoint.

steps.action: Submit the identity proofing form with a SQL injection payload in the 'Name' field.
steps.expected: The request is blocked by the WAF. A generic error page or 403 Forbidden response is returned. No database error is exposed.

steps.action: Submit the identity proofing form with a Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) payload in the 'Address' field.
steps.expected: The request is blocked by the WAF. The script is not executed in the browser, and the input is sanitized or rejected.

test_cases.title: Behavioral analytics flags abnormal typing speed during identity proofing
test_cases.preconditions: The VBP identity proofing form is accessible. Behavioral analytics is enabled to monitor user interaction patterns.
test_cases.test_inputs: A valid identity proofing form filled out with a typing speed significantly higher than human capability (e.g., via macro or auto-fill tool).
test_cases.assumptions: The system defines a threshold for 'abnormal' typing speed or interaction pattern that triggers a risk flag.

steps.action: Fill out the identity proofing form using an auto-fill tool or macro that inputs data at a speed exceeding the defined human threshold.
steps.expected: The system flags the session as high-risk based on behavioral analytics. The user may be challenged with additional verification steps (e.g., CAPTCHA or step-up authentication) or the session may be terminated.

steps.action: Review the risk assessment log for the session.
steps.expected: The log indicates that the session was flagged due to abnormal behavioral metrics (e.g., typing speed, mouse movement patterns).

test_cases.title: Network traffic analysis detects and mitigates DDoS-like traffic on identity proofing endpoint
test_cases.preconditions: The VBP identity proofing endpoint is accessible. Network traffic analysis tools are monitoring for volumetric attacks.
test_cases.test_inputs: A controlled burst of HTTP requests (e.g., 1000 requests/second) targeting the identity proofing endpoint from a single IP address.
test_cases.assumptions: The system has rate-limiting or DDoS mitigation rules configured for the identity proofing endpoint.

steps.action: Generate a high volume of concurrent requests to the identity proofing endpoint from a single source IP.
steps.expected: The network traffic analysis system detects the anomaly. The source IP is rate-limited or blocked. Legitimate users from other IPs can still access the service.

steps.action: Attempt to access the identity proofing endpoint from the blocked IP after the mitigation is triggered.
steps.expected: The request is rejected or delayed significantly, confirming that the mitigation is active for the offending source.

test_cases.title: Geçerli TOTP kodunun ilk kullanımında doğrulamanın başarılı olması
test_cases.preconditions: Kullanıcının iki faktörlü doğrulama (2FA) özelliği etkinleştirilmiştir ve geçerli bir TOTP kodu üretilmiştir.
test_cases.test_inputs: Geçerli bir TOTP kodu.

steps.action: Oturum açma veya işlem onaylama ekranında geçerli bir TOTP kodu girilir ve gönderilir.
steps.expected: Sistem TOTP kodunu kabul eder ve doğrulama işlemi başarılı olarak tamamlanır.

test_cases.title: Aynı geçerli TOTP kodunun ikinci kez kullanımında reddedilmesi
test_cases.preconditions: Kullanıcı, geçerli bir TOTP kodunu kullanarak başarılı bir doğrulama işlemi gerçekleştirmiştir. Kodun geçerlilik süresi henüz dolmamıştır.
test_cases.test_inputs: Daha önce kullanılmış olan aynı geçerli TOTP kodu.

steps.action: Yeni bir doğrulama isteğinde, daha önce kullanılmış olan aynı TOTP kodu girilir ve gönderilir.
steps.expected: Sistem TOTP kodunu reddeder ve 'kod zaten kullanıldı' veya benzeri bir hata mesajı gösterir. Doğrulama başarısız olur.

test_cases.title: Replacement recovery code issuance triggers notification
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with at least one active recovery code. The account is not locked.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid credentials for the company representative. A request to generate a replacement recovery code.
test_cases.assumptions: The system is configured to send notifications via a testable channel (e.g., email or in-app message) that can be intercepted or observed. The notification content structure follows NIST SP 800-63B-4 §4.6.

steps.action: Log in as the company representative.
steps.expected: The user is successfully authenticated and redirected to the account security or recovery settings page.

steps.action: Initiate the process to issue a replacement saved recovery code.
steps.expected: The system generates a new recovery code and displays it to the user (or provides a download link), indicating the old code is invalidated.

steps.action: Check the notification channel (e.g., email inbox or in-app notification center) associated with the account.
steps.expected: An account recovery notification is received. The notification indicates that a recovery code was replaced/issued, as per NIST SP 800-63B-4 §4.6 requirements (e.g., includes timestamp, action type, and potentially a link to review account activity).

test_cases.title: Notification content compliance check
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists. A test environment allows inspection of raw notification payloads or detailed logs.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid credentials. A request to generate a replacement recovery code.
test_cases.assumptions: The specific fields required by NIST SP 800-63B-4 §4.6 and internal spec §4.2.1.1 are known and can be verified in the notification payload.

steps.action: Log in as the company representative and issue a replacement recovery code.
steps.expected: The replacement code is successfully issued.

steps.action: Inspect the content of the sent account recovery notification.
steps.expected: The notification contains the specific elements required by NIST SP 800-63B-4 §4.6 (e.g., clear statement of the action 'recovery code replaced', timestamp of the event, and potentially the IP address or device info if specified in §4.2.1.1).

test_cases.title: Kurtarma kodu kullanıldıktan sonra geçersiz kılınması ve yeni kodun oluşturulması
test_cases.preconditions: Şirket temsilcisi için geçerli bir kurtarma kodu kayıtlıdır ve kullanıcı oturum açmıştır.
test_cases.test_inputs: Kayıtlı kurtarma kodu.
test_cases.assumptions: Sistem, NIST SP 800-63B-4 §4.2.1.1'e uygun olarak yeni bir kurtarma kodu üretme mekanizmasına sahiptir.

steps.action: Kayıtlı kurtarma kodu ile doğrulama işlemi yapılır.
steps.expected: Doğrulama başarılı olur ve kullanıcı işlemi tamamlar.

steps.action: Kullanılan kurtarma kodu ile tekrar doğrulama işlemi denenir.
steps.expected: Doğrulama başarısız olur, kodun geçersiz olduğu bildirilir.

steps.action: Şirket temsilcisinin kurtarma kodu listesi kontrol edilir.
steps.expected: Eski kodun yerine yeni bir kurtarma kodunun oluşturulduğu ve kaydedildiği görülür.

test_cases.title: Geçersiz kurtarma kodunun kullanılmaya çalışılması
test_cases.preconditions: Bir kurtarma kodu daha önce kullanılmış ve geçersiz kılınmıştır.
test_cases.test_inputs: Daha önce kullanılmış (geçersiz) kurtarma kodu.

steps.action: Geçersiz kılınmış kurtarma kodu ile doğrulama işlemi yapılır.
steps.expected: Sistem hata mesajı gösterir ve doğrulamayı reddeder.

test_cases.title: AAL2 ile başarılı kimlik doğrulama ve hesap erişimi

test_cases.title: AAL1 seviyesinde kimlik doğrulama denemesinin reddedilmesi

steps.expected: Hesap bilgilerine erişim sağlanamaz.

test_cases.title: Hesaba kayıtlı olmayan kimlik doğrulayıcı ile giriş denemesinin reddedilmesi

test_cases.test_inputs: Hesaba kayıtlı olmayan AAL2/AAL3 kimlik doğrulayıcısı.
